macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street suffers worst session since June as tech sell-off deepens
items.summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply, with major indexes declining at least 1% as technology shares came under renewed pressure. The sell-off was driven by concerns over AI spending, weaker company outlooks and stretched valuations.

items.title: Amazon gives cautious outlook despite strong cloud growth
items.summary: Amazon reported disappointing third-quarter results and issued a cautious outlook, while its cloud business delivered strong growth. The results added to concerns about the cost and payoff of major AI investments.

items.title: Fed officials favor further gradual rate increases
items.summary: Fed officials Lorie Logan, Tom Barkin and Alberto Musalem supported additional monetary tightening, with Logan arguing that at least two more 25-basis-point increases may be needed. Officials emphasized a gradual approach to managing inflation risks.

items.title: China discloses new overnight policy rate
items.summary: The People’s Bank of China publicly set its one-day reverse-repurchase rate at 1.25%, marking the first official disclosure of the rate. The move provides a new signal about China’s short-term monetary-policy stance.

items.title: China factory activity weakens
items.summary: China’s manufacturing activity declined as new export orders weakened, adding to concerns about external demand and the pace of the country’s industrial recovery.

items.title: ExxonMobil and Chevron beat third-quarter estimates
items.summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron exceeded third-quarter profit expectations, helped by higher prices and strong production. Energy stocks were among the stronger areas of earnings performance during the week.

items.title: Starbucks misses revenue forecasts despite resilient U.S. sales
items.summary: Starbucks said U.S. sales remained a bright spot, but quarterly revenue fell short of analyst expectations. The result highlights uneven performance across consumer-facing companies amid broader market volatility.

items.title: European Central Bank president resigns
items.summary: The European Central Bank’s head resigned, allowing EU leaders to select a successor before France’s presidential election. The leadership change could affect expectations for the euro area’s future monetary-policy direction.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance reports $6.3 billion security breach
items.summary: Binance reported a major security incident involving unauthorized withdrawals across multiple chains, temporarily suspending deposits and withdrawals. The exchange said it would cover user losses, while approximately $3 billion in assets were reportedly frozen.[1][4][7]

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $77,000 after Binance breach
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped as much as 3.1% to approximately $76,300 before partially recovering, while Ethereum and other major tokens also declined amid renewed concerns about exchange security.[1][6][7]

items.title: Attackers use Tron and DeFi to move stolen Binance funds
items.summary: Blockchain investigators said suspected attackers used Tron to swap assets into stablecoins and routed funds through DeFi protocols, complicating efforts by centralized issuers to freeze them.[5]

items.title: CFTC develops voluntary federal registration for crypto exchanges
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is reportedly developing a voluntary registration framework for crypto exchanges using existing authority while broader market-structure legislation remains pending.[4]

items.title: NYSE owner partners on regulated Hyperliquid perpetuals venue
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange partnered with trade[XYZ] to develop a regulated U.S. perpetual-futures venue on Hyperliquid and make a strategic investment in the company.[4]

items.title: France advances OECD crypto-asset reporting framework
items.summary: France’s Senate adopted legislation ratifying the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, ahead of planned international data exchanges beginning in 2027.[3]

items.title: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs record fresh inflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs received approximately $440.8 million in net inflows from October 26 through 29, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for about $410.6 million.[4]

items.title: Curve StableSwap launches on Stellar
items.summary: Curve Finance deployed StableSwap on Stellar, its first deployment outside the Ethereum Virtual Machine ecosystem, with an FXSwap launch planned next.[3]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: AI spending concerns trigger sharp tech-stock selloff
items.summary: Technology stocks fell sharply as investors questioned whether major companies’ debt-funded AI infrastructure spending can justify current valuations. The Nasdaq dropped about 2.8%–2.9%, while Amazon, Intel, Nvidia and other AI-related companies declined.[11][13]

items.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back standardized AI scraping opt-out
items.summary: The four companies pledged to support a common mechanism allowing publishers and websites to tell AI crawlers not to collect their content for model training. Rollouts are expected over the coming months and during 2027.[14]

items.title: Foxconn signals forthcoming collaboration with OpenAI
items.summary: Foxconn Chairman Young Liu said the electronics manufacturer is working toward a new partnership with OpenAI, following an earlier agreement focused on data-center racks, components and AI hardware.[17]

items.title: Anthropic expands Claude restrictions on reverse engineering
items.summary: Developers report that Claude Code and Claude Opus 5.5 are refusing some video-game cloning and reverse-engineering requests, with complaints that the restrictions also affect legitimate development and troubleshooting work.[15]

items.title: AI developer platforms face wave of credential-abuse incidents
items.summary: A security review reported nine AI developer platforms disclosing incidents during October, including cases involving stolen credentials and unauthorized model usage that generated more than $100,000 in charges.[12]

items.title: Mistral releases improved Large 4 model weights
items.summary: Mistral released updated Large 4 weights after a public preview. The multimodal model includes three reasoning modes and is designed to run on an organization’s own infrastructure.[20]

items.title: Anthropic files for planned public offering
items.summary: Anthropic filed an S-1 registration statement ahead of a potential IPO, as investor scrutiny intensifies around the capital requirements and profitability prospects of frontier AI companies.[16][19]
